input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: § 28.1 selects Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is effectively an exclusive foreign venue — walk-away territory. It also directly conflicts with § 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. The minimal fix changes only the jurisdiction and forum words in § 28.1 to New York law and New York County courts, reaching the preferred position and resolving the internal conflict; § 28.2's carve-out for urgent injunctive relief and § 28.3's escalation step are left intact. No arbitration clause appears elsewhere in the document.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Singapore to New York and align exclusive venue with § 28.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Singapore to New York and aligned the exclusive forum with the New York County courts already named in § 28.2, which currently conflicts with this clause. Our playbook requires New York law and venue (Delaware, California or England and Wales are acceptable alternatives).

ops.oldText: governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction
ops.newText: governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction
